promise_band.headline: You will hear back from us
promise_band.body: Ask around Lackawanna County and you will hear the same story about roofers: nobody answers, nobody returns the message, and the estimate never arrives. We built our schedule around not being that company. You get a person, a date, and a written number — and if we cannot help, we say so instead of going quiet.

signature_system.headline: How we handle a storm damage claim
signature_system.intro: Hail, wind, and tree damage are where homeowners lose the most money — and where most contractors stop being useful. Here is exactly what we do, and why each part matters.

blocks.title: We document what actually happened
blocks.body: A full inspection of every slope before anyone disputes anything. Undocumented damage is damage your policy will not pay for, so we photograph it while the date of loss is still clear.

blocks.title: We work directly with your insurance company
blocks.body: This is the part that saves you the time and the frustration. Our project managers deal with the carrier, so you are not the one translating between an adjuster and a roofer.

blocks.title: We are paid the same either way
blocks.body: Our fee does not change based on what your insurer pays out. That is precisely why our project managers can push for the reimbursement you are actually owed without it being a sales tactic — a point one of our customers made better than we can.

blocks.title: We finish it on time and on budget
blocks.body: Hail, wind, or tree damage, the repair gets done to your satisfaction with solutions built to last. Most of our storm replacements are complete in one to two days once materials are on site.

signature_system.steps_title: What that looks like on your calendar

seo_body.headline: What a Northeastern Pennsylvania roof is up against
paragraphs: Roofs in Lackawanna, Luzerne, Wayne and Pike counties take a specific kind of beating. Freeze-thaw cycling works water into every seam and then widens it overnight. Ice dams build at the eaves on homes with older attic insulation and push meltwater back under the shingles. Summer hail and straight-line wind add their own damage on top, and most of it does not announce itself until there is a stain on a bedroom ceiling.

The harder problem is usually the claim, not the roof. Homeowners tell the same story: an adjuster who moves fast, an estimate that comes back short, and nobody in their corner who can explain what should have been on it. That is the part we handle directly. Our project managers deal with your carrier, and because our fee is the same regardless of what the policy pays, there is no incentive on our side to inflate anything — only to make sure the real damage is on the paperwork.

We work across Lackawanna, Luzerne, Wayne, Pike, Wyoming, Monroe and Susquehanna counties from our office in Jessup, and across Baltimore City and seventeen Maryland counties from our Baltimore office. If your roof is showing its age or your neighborhood just took a storm, start with a free in-home estimate — it costs nothing and you get a straight answer either way.

faqs.q: What does an estimate cost, and am I committing to anything?
faqs.a: Nothing, and no. Our in-home estimate is free and carries no obligation. We inspect the property, then sit down with you and go through what we found and what each option costs — because we would rather you understand exactly what you are getting for your money than sign something you have not read.

faqs.q: Someone knocked on my door after the storm and said I need a new roof. Do I?
faqs.a: Maybe, and maybe not. After hail or high wind, crews from out of the area work NEPA neighborhoods, and not all of them are careful about what they tell homeowners. Get a second opinion from a company with a local address you can drive to. Ours is 1 Keystone Place in Jessup, and the second opinion is free.

faqs.q: Do you handle the insurance claim, or do I?
faqs.a: You file the claim; we do the heavy lifting after that. We work directly with your insurance company so you are not stuck translating between an adjuster and a roofer. Our fee does not change based on what the policy pays, so our only job in that conversation is making sure the damage that is actually there ends up on the paperwork.

faqs.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
faqs.a: Most of our residential replacements are finished in one to two days once materials are on site. A 28-square roof in Clarks Green went start to finish in a single day; a 53-square hail replacement in Dickson City took two. Steep pitch, multiple layers, or decking that needs re-sheeting can add time, and we tell you up front when we expect that.

faqs.q: What warranty comes with the roof?
faqs.a: We are an Owens Corning Preferred Contractor, which is what allows us to offer the longest warranty available on the materials. That coverage is backed by the manufacturer rather than by us alone, so it does not depend on any contractor still being in business years from now. Your project manager goes through the specific warranty terms with you before work begins.

Yes. A roof rarely fails at a convenient moment, so we offer financing options alongside every estimate and options at more than one price point. Ask your project manager during the in-home visit and we will lay out what is available.

From Jessup we serve Lackawanna, Luzerne, Wayne, Pike, Wyoming, Monroe and Susquehanna counties. From our Baltimore office we serve Baltimore City plus Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Frederick, Dorchester, Harford, Garrett, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's and Queen Anne's counties.

faqs.q: What will my yard look like when you leave?
faqs.a: Clean. It is the thing our customers bring up most without being asked — debris hauled, nails swept, landscaping intact. One Scranton homeowner put it as leaving the job site as clean or cleaner than they found it, and that is the standard we hold the crews to.
